newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Tuntex gives Taipei final say on S.Africa project.
newsitem.headline: Tuntex gives Taipei final say on S.Africa project.

text.p: Taiwan's Tuntex Distinct Corp said on Thursday it would respect the Taiwan government's wishes in deciding whether to continue a US$3.0 billion petrochemical project in South Africa.
"For this petrochemical plant project, the Tuntex group will decide whether to go ahead or stop depending on the (Taiwan) government's policy," Tuntex said in a statement.

Tuntex was responding to South Africa's decision on Wednesday to drop diplomatic ties with Taiwan in 1997 in favour of the island's arch rival in Beijing, a move that raised questions about whether Taiwan investors would continue what had been their strong economic support of South Africa.
"We will full back the government's effort to extend our foreign ties," Tuntex said.
Taiwan officials have said they did not view Pretoria's decision as final and would press South Africa to reconsider.
Taiwan Foreign Minister John Chang, addressing reporters on Thursday morning, said Taipei would review the island's South Africa projects before making any final decisions.
"In the next 12 months, we have a plan to do an overall review, including economic cooperation projects," Chang said.
Taiwan has sought to use its economic muscle to counter rival China's efforts to isolate it diplomatically.
Beijing has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949 and pledges to retake the island, by force if necessary.
Nearly 300 Taiwan businesses have operations in South Africa with investments topping $1.5 billion.
